title: XML External Entity Injection Security Analysis

vulnerability.name: XML External Entity Injection
vulnerability.description: Attacks against applications that parse XML input
vulnerability.impact: File disclosure, SSRF, denial of service, or data theft
vulnerability.mitigation: Disable DTDs and external entities in XML parsers, validate and sanitize inputs

findings.title: Vulnerable XML parsing
findings.explanation: The contract uses a DTD without proper entity restrictions, making it vulnerable to XML External Entity Injection.
findings.impact: Potential SSRF or file disclosure attacks
exploitation_steps: Attacker sends a malicious XML payload as the _weiToWithdraw value
findings.exploitation_conditions: The contract uses a DTD without proper entity restrictions.
findings.remediation: Disable DTDs and external entities in XML parsers

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The Log contract uses a script to execute the AddMessage function with user-provided input (_am) without proper validation or sanitization.
findings.impact: Remote code execution and potential data theft
findings.execution_path_diagram:
AddMessage(msg.sender, _am, "CashOut")
Call contract at /CashOut
Execute function with user-provided input
exploitation_steps: Attackers manipulate the value of _am to execute arbitrary code
Send a maliciously crafted _am value to trigger the attack
findings.exploitation_conditions: The caller has sufficient authorization and the contract is in a vulnerable state
findings.remediation: Properly validate and sanitize user input, such as using require or assert statements to enforce input constraints.

findings.title: XML External Entity Injection
findings.explanation: The _walletLibrary.delegatecall(msg.data) call does not validate the input data, allowing an attacker to inject XML External Entities.
findings.impact: File disclosure, SSRF, denial of service, or data theft
exploitation_steps: Attackers inject an XML External Entity into msg.data
findings.exploitation_conditions: msg.sender is authenticated and has access to delegatecall
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize input data, including msg.data
findings.secure_code_example: function hasConfirmed(bytes32 _operation, address _owner) external constant returns (bool) { if (_walletLibrary.delegatecall(msg.data) == 0x0) { return true; } else { return false; }}

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: This function allows an attacker to inject external entities by manipulating the `_operation` parameter.
findings.impact: Potential for data theft or denial of service
findings.execution_path_diagram:
getOwner(uint ownerIndex) -> revoke(bytes32 _operation) -> Revoke(msg.sender, _operation)
execute(address _to, uint _value, bytes _data) -> confirm(bytes32 o_hash) -> revoke(o_hash)
exploitation_steps: Manipulate the `_operation` parameter to inject external entities.
Send a request with an injected entity (e.g. `<x>`) to the `/revoke` endpoint.
findings.exploitation_conditions: Access to the `/revoke` endpoint while authenticated.
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize the `_operation` parameter to prevent external entity injection.

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The `m_pending[_operation]` object is not properly sanitized, allowing for XML External Entity Injection attacks.
findings.impact: Potential data theft or file disclosure
exploitation_steps: Allow XML External Entity Injection via m_pending[_operation]
findings.remediation: Sanitize and validate user input for _operation in confirmAndCheck
